subject: Political Science (Code: 323)
past_paper_reference: CUET UG Political Science Past Papers (2022-2024)

questions.question: The first general elections in independent India were conducted between October 1951 and which month of 1952?
questions.explanation: India's first general elections began in October 1951 and were completed in February 1952, though they are commonly referred to as the 1952 elections.

questions.question: In the first Lok Sabha elections of 1952, how many seats out of 489 were won by the Indian National Congress, securing an overwhelming majority?
questions.explanation: The Congress won 364 of the 489 seats in the first Lok Sabha, finishing vastly ahead of any other political contender.

questions.question: The dairy cooperative movement known as 'Amul' originated in which town of Gujarat?
questions.explanation: Amul was founded in 1946 in Anand, Gujarat, developing the cooperative dairy model that inspired India's nationwide White Revolution.

questions.question: The Asian Relations Conference, representing the early vision of Asian resurgence and solidarity, was convened in New Delhi in March 1947 under the leadership of:
questions.explanation: Five months before India attained independence, Jawaharlal Nehru convened the Asian Relations Conference in New Delhi in March 1947 to unite Asian nations.

questions.topic: Challenge to and Restoration of Congress System
questions.question: Which iconic campaign slogan was coined by Indira Gandhi during the 1971 Lok Sabha elections to appeal directly to the underprivileged masses?
questions.explanation: Indira Gandhi countered the opposition's negative slogan 'Indira Hatao' with the transformative positive slogan 'Garibi Hatao' in the 1971 elections.

questions.question: In March 1974, Jayaprakash Narayan came out of political retirement to lead the mass student agitation in which state?
questions.explanation: In March 1974, students in Bihar invited Jayaprakash Narayan to lead their agitation against rising prices, food scarcity, corruption, and unemployment.

questions.question: Following the signing of the Mizo Peace Accord in 1986, Mizoram was formally conferred full statehood in which year?
questions.explanation: Mizoram was inaugurated as the 23rd state of the Indian Union in February 1987 following the successful implementation of the 1986 accord.

questions.question: The militant socio-political organisation named Dalit Panthers was established in 1972 by young Dalit activists in which state?
questions.explanation: Dalit Panthers was founded in Mumbai, Maharashtra, in 1972 by writers and activists including Namdeo Dhasal and Arjun Dangle, inspired by the Black Panther movement in the US.

questions.question: In which year did the B.P. Mandal Commission submit its comprehensive report to the Union Government outlining reservations for Other Backward Classes?
questions.explanation: The Second Backward Classes Commission (Mandal Commission) submitted its report in December 1980, recommending 27% quota for OBCs.

questions.question: The first National Democratic Alliance (NDA) government that completed a full five-year term in office (1999-2004) was headed by Prime Minister:
questions.explanation: Atal Bihari Vajpayee led the NDA coalition government formed in October 1999, which became the first non-Congress coalition to complete a full 5-year tenure.

questions.topic: Cold War Era and Non-aligned Movement
questions.question: In 1949, the Cold War division of Germany led to the creation of two separate states: the Federal Republic of Germany (FRG) in the west and which state in the east?
questions.explanation: In 1949, Germany was partitioned into the Western-allied Federal Republic of Germany (FRG) and the Soviet-dominated German Democratic Republic (GDR).

questions.question: Which historic treaty signed in 1957 established the European Economic Community (EEC) and the European Atomic Energy Community (Euratom)?
questions.explanation: The Treaty of Rome was signed on 25 March 1957 by France, West Germany, Italy, Belgium, the Netherlands, and Luxembourg, creating the European Economic Community.

questions.question: Prior to the independence of India, the princely state of Travancore announced its intention to remain an independent sovereign state under the influence of its Diwan:
questions.explanation: Sir C.P. Ramaswamy Aiyar, Diwan of Travancore, initially declared that Travancore would remain an independent sovereign entity, but relented following public agitation and diplomatic pressure from Sardar Patel.

questions.question: In the 1957 state legislative assembly elections, which political party won 60 out of 126 seats in Kerala and formed the world's first democratically elected communist ministry?
questions.explanation: In 1957, the CPI won a majority with support of independents in Kerala, and E.M.S. Namboodiripad formed the first democratically elected communist government.

questions.question: The First Five Year Plan (1951-1956) was drafted by a group of economists prominently including which young planner who urged India to 'hasten slowly' for the first two decades?
questions.explanation: K.N. Raj was one of the primary young architects of the First Plan, arguing that India needed to step up agricultural savings gradually rather than risking hyperinflation.

questions.question: India carried out its first nuclear explosion at Pokhran in Rajasthan in May 1974, which the Government of India officially classified as a:
questions.explanation: India maintained that the May 1974 Pokhran-I test was a 'Peaceful Nuclear Explosion' (PNE) conducted for civilian energy and scientific research.

questions.topic: Challenge to and Restoration of Congress System
questions.question: In Uttar Pradesh, the first non-Congress Samyukta Vidhayak Dal (SVD) government formed in 1967 was headed by which veteran peasant leader who defected from the Congress?
questions.explanation: Charan Singh left the Congress to lead the Samyukta Vidhayak Dal coalition in Uttar Pradesh, serving as Chief Minister in 1967.

questions.question: To prevent future misuse of emergency powers, the 44th Constitutional Amendment Act (1978) amended Article 352 by substituting the phrase 'internal disturbance' with:
questions.explanation: The Janata Party's 44th Amendment Act of 1978 replaced the vague term 'internal disturbance' with 'armed rebellion' as the only domestic condition for proclaiming an Emergency.

questions.question: During the six-year Assam Movement (1979-1985), the All Assam Students Union (AASU) organized protests centered around the demand for the '3 Ds', which stood for:
options: A) Defend, Demarcate, and Disarm border zones
B) Demolish, Disperse, and Denounce infiltrators
C) Detect, Delete, and Deport illegal foreigners
D) Determine, Decentralize, and Develop tribal areas
questions.explanation: AASU campaigned for the '3 Ds': Detection of illegal foreign nationals, Deletion of their names from the electoral rolls, and Deportation back across the border.

questions.question: A distinctive institutional feature of the Bharatiya Kisan Union (BKU) that enabled high peasant mobilisation in western Uttar Pradesh was its reliance on traditional clan networks known as:
questions.explanation: The BKU effectively utilized kinship networks and traditional clan assemblies (Khap panchayats) of western UP and Haryana to mobilize agrarian communities.

questions.question: The diverse parties constituting the United Front government in 1996 agreed upon a governing agenda to coordinate their policy priorities, titled the:
questions.explanation: The United Front framed a 'Common Minimum Programme' (CMP) in 1996 to harmonize policy priorities across its left, centrist, and regional constituent parties.

questions.question: In July 1991, the New Economic Policy inaugurating LPG (Liberalisation, Privatisation, and Globalisation) was introduced by the Narasimha Rao government under Union Finance Minister:
questions.explanation: Dr. Manmohan Singh served as Union Finance Minister in 1991 and presented the budget that dismantled the License Raj and initiated sweeping structural adjustment reforms.

questions.topic: Cold War Era and Non-aligned Movement
questions.question: The Limited Test Ban Treaty (LTBT) signed in Moscow in August 1963 prohibited nuclear weapon tests in which environments?
options: A) Underground only, permitting atmospheric detonations
B) Exclusively in the polar regions of the Arctic and Antarctic
C) In the atmosphere, in outer space, and underwater
D) In all environments without exception, including underground tests
questions.explanation: The LTBT (1963) banned nuclear weapon testing in the atmosphere, in outer space, and underwater, though it still permitted underground nuclear detonations.

questions.question: Following the collapse of the Soviet Union, the Russian Federation engaged in protracted military conflicts to suppress violent secessionist insurgencies in which North Caucasus republics?
questions.explanation: Russia fought devastating wars in Chechnya (1994-1996 and 1999-2009) and Dagestan to crush Islamist and separatist armed rebellions in the North Caucasus.

questions.question: In 1999, NATO launched a 78-day bombing campaign against the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia during the Kosovo crisis without UN Security Council authorization, code-named:
questions.explanation: Operation Allied Force was the NATO bombing of Serbian and Yugoslav targets from March to June 1999 to halt ethnic cleansing of Albanians in Kosovo.

questions.question: The 'ASEAN Way' is widely described in international relations as a distinctive diplomatic model characterized by:
options: A) A rigid supranational legal court with mandatory judicial penalties
B) An informal, non-confrontational, and consensus-based process of regional cooperation
C) A collective military alliance treaty with mutual defense commitments
D) A tariff-free union with a single centralized executive presidency
questions.explanation: The 'ASEAN Way' emphasizes national sovereignty, informal consultations, consensus-building, and non-interference, avoiding formal legalistic confrontations.

questions.question: In 1972, the People's Republic of China broke its long diplomatic isolation by establishing bilateral ties with the United States following the historic visit to Beijing by President:
questions.explanation: President Richard Nixon traveled to China in February 1972, ending decades of diplomatic estrangement and opening the way for China's international integration.

questions.question: Article X of the SAARC Charter incorporates two fundamental operational principles: decisions at all levels must be taken on the basis of unanimity, and:
options: A) All member states must adopt an identical currency within a decade
B) Every dispute must be submitted to binding arbitration by India
C) Military joint exercises must be conducted annually in Kathmandu
D) Bilateral and contentious issues shall be excluded from the deliberations
questions.explanation: Article X(2) of the SAARC Charter explicitly stipulates that bilateral and contentious issues must be excluded from SAARC meetings to preserve regional consensus.

questions.question: The agreement establishing the South Asian Free Trade Area (SAFTA) to reduce customs duties on traded goods was signed by SAARC leaders in 2004 in which city?
questions.explanation: SAFTA was signed at the 12th SAARC Summit in Islamabad in January 2004 and entered into force on 1 January 2006.

questions.question: The international human rights NGO Human Rights Watch was originally established in 1978 under the name 'Helsinki Watch' to monitor compliance with the:
questions.explanation: Helsinki Watch was established in 1978 to monitor human rights compliance in the Soviet bloc under the 1975 Helsinki Accords, later evolving into Human Rights Watch.

questions.question: A decisive institutional advancement of the World Trade Organization (WTO) over its predecessor, GATT, was the creation of:
options: A) A permanent UN standing army to enforce trade agreements
B) A single unified global currency pegged to the US dollar
C) A binding, rules-based Dispute Settlement Mechanism (DSM)
D) An executive veto held exclusively by developing countries
questions.explanation: Unlike GATT's voluntary consultations, the WTO instituted a Dispute Settlement Mechanism with appellate review whose rulings cannot be unilaterally blocked by a losing party.

questions.question: In the traditional conception of national security, the greatest and most acute danger to a sovereign state is understood as:
options: A) Global climate change and rising ocean levels
B) Fluctuations in currency exchange rates on international markets
C) The emergence of chronic non-communicable diseases
D) External military attack from another state threatening its sovereignty and territorial integrity
questions.explanation: Traditional security centers on the state, identifying military aggression by other nation-states against its territory, population, or sovereignty as the core threat.

questions.question: The influential 1972 report published by the Club of Rome that dramatized the dangers of exponential population and industrial growth on planet Earth's finite resources was titled:
questions.explanation: The Club of Rome commissioned MIT researchers to model resource constraints, publishing 'The Limits to Growth' in 1972, highlighting impending limits to industrial civilization.

questions.question: In the context of global environmental governance, indigenous populations assert special claims over their ancestral territories based on their status as:
options: A) Exclusive industrial corporate concessionaires appointed by the United Nations
B) Descendants of peoples who inhabited a territory prior to colonization, retaining distinct cultural ties to ancestral land and ecosystems
C) Immigrant communities that arrived during post-industrial urbanization
D) Private corporate landowners holding municipal commercial leases
questions.explanation: The UN defines indigenous populations as descendants of the original inhabitants of a country who maintain distinct linguistic, social, and spiritual attachments to their ancestral lands.

questions.question: In which Indian city was the fourth meeting of the World Social Forum (WSF) convened in January 2004, marking its first session held outside of Brazil?
questions.explanation: The 4th World Social Forum took place in Mumbai in January 2004, drawing over 100,000 activists from around the world to protest neo-liberal policies.

questions.question: Madras State was officially renamed 'Tamil Nadu' in January 1969 following a sustained movement and the passage of a resolution under the Chief Ministership of:
questions.explanation: DMK leader C.N. Annadurai led the Madras Legislative Assembly to adopt a resolution in July 1967 to rename the state 'Tamil Nadu', which officially took effect on 14 January 1969.

questions.question: Political scientist Rajni Kothari conceptualized the first two decades of India's post-independence party landscape as the 'Congress System'. This system was characterized as:
options: A) A dominant umbrella party functioning as a system of internal factions, accommodating diverse interests while opposition parties acted as pressure groups from the periphery.
B) A totalitarian single-party dictatorship prohibiting opposition parties by constitutional decree.
C) A classical two-party Westminster alternation between Congress and the Communist Party.
D) A decentralized federal anarchy lacking any national consensus on democratic rules.
questions.explanation: Rajni Kothari argued that the Congress represented a consensus system with internal factions balancing regional, ideological, and social claims, while opposition parties influenced policy by exerting pressure on factions within Congress.

questions.question: In 1944, a group of prominent Indian industrialists drafted 'A Plan of Economic Development for India' (the Bombay Plan). What was the core proposal of this historic document?
options: A) It demanded an entirely laissez-faire capitalist economy with zero government ownership or regulation.
B) It advocated significant state intervention, public investment in infrastructure and heavy industry, and economic planning to build national industrial capability.
C) It called for the immediate nationalization of all private textile mills and agrarian land without compensation.
D) It insisted that India remain a pastoral agricultural dependency importing all machinery from Great Britain.
questions.explanation: The Bombay Plan (signed by J.R.D. Tata, G.D. Birla, Purshotamdas Thakurdas, and others) acknowledged that private capital was inadequate for massive infrastructure and heavy industries, hence urging state planning and public capital formation.

questions.question: Which diplomatic breakthrough in July 1971 created a US-China-Pakistan strategic nexus that hastened India's signing of the Treaty of Peace, Friendship and Cooperation with the Soviet Union?
options: A) The signing of the Sino-Pak Free Trade Agreement in Islamabad
B) The deployment of the US Seventh Fleet to the Bay of Bengal during the Rann of Kutch dispute
C) Henry Kissinger's secret mission to Beijing via Pakistan to arrange President Nixon's visit to China
D) China's formal admission into the Southeast Asia Treaty Organization (SEATO)
questions.explanation: In July 1971, US National Security Advisor Henry Kissinger made a secret trip from Rawalpindi to Beijing, signaling a dramatic US-China alignment facilitated by Pakistan, creating an acute security encirclement for India.

questions.topic: Challenge to and Restoration of Congress System
questions.question: Which of the following events directly precipitated Indira Gandhi's open rebellion against the Congress Syndicate during the 1969 presidential election?
options: A) Morarji Desai's defection to form the Bharatiya Lok Dal in the Lok Sabha.
B) The Supreme Court's declaration that the 1967 general elections were invalid.
C) The refusal of the Election Commission to grant the Congress election symbol to Indira Gandhi.
D) The Syndicate's nomination of Neelam Sanjiva Reddy against Indira Gandhi's wishes, prompting her to back Vice-President V.V. Giri as an independent candidate calling for a 'conscience vote'.
questions.explanation: After the death of President Zakir Husain, the Syndicate chose Sanjiva Reddy as the official party candidate. Indira Gandhi covertly backed V.V. Giri, stripped Morarji Desai of the Finance portfolio, nationalized 14 banks, and urged lawmakers to vote according to conscience.

questions.question: In April 1973, following the landmark Supreme Court ruling in the Kesavananda Bharati case, the Union Government deviated from the established convention of appointing the senior-most judge as Chief Justice of India by superseding three judges to appoint:
questions.explanation: The government bypassed senior Justices J.M. Shelat, K.S. Hegde, and A.N. Grover (who ruled against the government in the Kesavananda case) to appoint Justice A.N. Ray as Chief Justice on 25 April 1973.

questions.question: The 1952 Delhi Agreement concluded between Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru and Jammu & Kashmir Prime Minister Sheikh Abdullah provided that:
options: A) Jammu & Kashmir would merge unconditionally into Punjab without any distinct constitutional status.

B) Jammu & Kashmir would have its own state flag, the state legislature would control residency and citizenship rights, while the President of India's jurisdiction over defense and foreign affairs was affirmed.
C) The Supreme Court of India would have zero appellate jurisdiction over any civil or criminal matters in the state forever.
D) All Union revenue taxation laws would automatically apply to the state without ratification by its Constituent Assembly.
questions.explanation: The 1952 Delhi Agreement gave constitutional shape to Article 370, retaining a separate state flag and autonomous citizenship/land ownership laws for state subjects while placing external affairs and defense under the Union.

questions.question: The National Fishworkers' Forum (NFF), an umbrella network representing traditional artisanal fishermen across India, led major national agitations in the 1990s against:
options: A) The establishment of wildlife marine sanctuaries in coastal Tamil Nadu.
B) The mandatory requirement for artisanal fishermen to join registered state cooperatives.
C) The Union government's deep-sea fishing policy that licensed joint-venture commercial mechanised trawlers in Indian territorial waters.
D) The complete ban on exporting dried shrimp and tuna to Southeast Asia.
questions.explanation: The NFF mobilised thousands of traditional fishworkers against the 1991 deep-sea fishing policy which allowed multinational industrial vessels to operate in the Exclusive Economic Zone, depleting marine stocks.

questions.question: In the landmark Indira Sawhney v. Union of India (1992) judgment on OBC reservations, the Supreme Court ruled that:
options: A) All reservations based on caste were unconstitutional and must be replaced entirely by an economic income criterion.
B) Reservations in central government appointments could be raised up to 80% without any constitutional barrier.
C) The Mandal Commission had no statutory authority and its recommendations were completely struck down.
D) The 27% quota for OBCs was constitutionally valid, but total reservations must not exceed 50% and the economically advanced 'creamy layer' among OBCs must be excluded.
questions.explanation: A nine-judge bench in Indira Sawhney (1992) upheld the 27% OBC reservation subject to excluding the 'creamy layer' and capping total quotas at 50% except in extraordinary circumstances.

questions.question: The violent disintegration of Yugoslavia in the early 1990s was marked by the declaration of independence in 1991 by which of the following constituent republics?
questions.explanation: In June 1991, Slovenia and Croatia declared independence from the Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, initiating military clashes and the subsequent unraveling of the federation.

questions.question: Political scientist Joseph Nye introduced the concepts of 'Hard Power' and 'Soft Power' to analyze international hegemony. In this analytical framework, 'Soft Power' refers to:
options: A) The deployment of long-range cruise missiles and naval carrier battle groups.
B) The ability of a nation to shape the preferences of others through appeal, cultural attraction, ideology, and values rather than coercion or economic inducements.
C) The enforcement of punitive international trade tariffs and financial blockades.
D) The distribution of nuclear warheads to regional military treaty partners.
questions.explanation: Joseph Nye defined soft power as getting others to desire the outcomes you desire through attraction rather than coercion (hard military power) or payments (economic power).

questions.sub_topic: European Union Divergence over Iraq War
questions.question: The 2003 US invasion of Iraq demonstrated internal divisions within the European Union when:
options: A) All European Union members deployed combat battalions under a unified EU military command.
B) The European Union voted unanimously to impose economic sanctions against the United States.
C) Britain and Spain joined the US-led 'coalition of the willing', while France and Germany vehemently opposed the military operation.
D) Eastern European nations expelled all US military garrisons from NATO airbases.
questions.explanation: The 2003 Iraq War divided the EU: British PM Tony Blair and Spanish PM Jose Maria Aznar backed the invasion, whereas French President Jacques Chirac and German Chancellor Gerhard Schröder opposed it.

questions.question: The 'Uniting for Peace' Resolution (Resolution 377A), adopted by the United Nations General Assembly in November 1950 during the Korean crisis, provides that:
options: A) The five permanent members of the Security Council forfeit their veto power during any wartime emergency.
B) The International Court of Justice can automatically issue binding war declarations against any aggressor state.
C) The Secretary-General can independently deploy nuclear forces to suppress interstate warfare.

D) If the Security Council fails to exercise its primary responsibility for international peace due to lack of unanimity among permanent members, the General Assembly can consider the matter and recommend collective measures.
questions.explanation: Resolution 377A (Uniting for Peace) was passed in 1950 to bypass Soviet vetoes during the Korean War, empowering the General Assembly to recommend collective security measures when the Security Council is deadlocked.

questions.question: In non-traditional security discourse, the broad concept of 'Human Security' encompasses two core dimensions popularized by the 1994 UNDP Human Development Report:
options: A) 'Freedom from fear' (protection from violence and conflict) and 'freedom from want' (protection from poverty, hunger, and disease)
B) 'Freedom of speech' and 'freedom of capital movement'
C) 'Freedom of high-seas navigation' and 'freedom of airspace surveillance'
D) 'Freedom to build nuclear weapons' and 'freedom to form bilateral alliances'
questions.explanation: The 1994 UNDP Report defined Human Security along two axes: 'freedom from fear' (physical safety against violence) and 'freedom from want' (economic and social security against deprivation).

questions.question: The 1997 Kyoto Protocol to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC) established legally binding emissions reduction targets exclusively for:
options: A) Developing nations exclusively, exempting industrialized Western states.
B) All member countries of the United Nations in an identical proportion.
C) Annex I developed countries, reflecting their historical responsibility for global industrial greenhouse emissions.
D) Landlocked nations with tropical rainforest canopies.
questions.explanation: Under the principle of Common But Differentiated Responsibilities (CBDR), the Kyoto Protocol mandated emission cuts only for developed nations (Annex I), exempting developing countries like India and China from binding reductions during the first commitment period.
